title: fix(app-shell,data-objectstack): one request per metadata URL across the provider and the adapter cache (objectui#13044)
body:
Fixes #13044
Clause-②: no

## What changes

One page open now asks the server for one metadata URL once, whichever of the two client caches asks first.

**Object documents (`GET /api/v1/meta/object/NAME`).** `MetadataProvider`'s published by-name `object` read now goes through the adapter's existing public `getObjectSchema`. The provider (page object scope, `useMetadataItem`) and the adapter's readers (record form, `useSettledSchema`, the field widgets) share one `MetadataCache` entry, one in-flight request, and the revalidating `cache: 'no-cache'` fetch.

**The published view list (`GET /api/v1/meta/view`): shared in flight only.**
- It has one `MetadataCache` key, `list:view`. The adapter wraps its own client's bare `meta.getItems('view')`, the same way it already wraps `meta.saveItem` for advisories.
- A call joins a request that is already in flight. Nothing is stored, so `listViews` stays uncached and a refresh re-reads it.
- Measured console order (pin): the eager read lands first, then `listViews` and `listViewOverrides` share one request. That is **2** `meta/view` requests per open, down from 3. A reader asking during the eager read joins it, for 1.

## Which shape, and why (the ruling asked)

I picked the narrower of the two shapes for each resource:

- **Objects: the provider reads through the data source's existing cached method** (`getObjectSchema`). I did not do the reverse (routing the SDK's `getItem('object', NAME)` into the adapter cache). That would hand every `getClient().meta.getItem('object', …)` caller the adapter's normalized document. `MetadataService.saveFields` uses that read as the base of a read-modify-write, so the adapter's normalization would leak into the saved body.
- **The view list: the adapter's client joins in-flight reads.** There is no settled entry, per seat ruling `6268839381` (d). A settled list would need every refresh and every in-SPA view write to drop it, and two of those paths are outside this surface:
  - `refreshData` in `ObjectView.tsx`;
  - the `MetadataClient` publish and save paths in `views/metadata-admin` and `views/studio-design`.

  The residual second request is the follow-up card. The client wrap adds no member.

## What each reader sees (unchanged)

- **Provider object readers:**
  - They get a `structuredClone` of the adapter's answer, wrapped back in the `{ item }` envelope, so `extractItem` and the objectui#7650 normalization run exactly as before.
  - The copy carries no sortability projection, because the symbol is non-enumerable and `structuredClone` drops it. A change made to one copy never reaches the other.
  - A 404 reaches the provider's catch as the transport's own error, taken from `MetadataNotFoundError`'s `originalError`, so `isMetaItemAbsentError` still tells an absence from a failure.
- **Adapter readers:** unchanged. They keep the revalidation, the sortability projection and the error wrapping.
- **View-list readers:** every caller gets its own copy of the shared answer. A raw client caller is never answered from the settled entry. It only joins a request that is on the wire.

## Invalidation

- `MetadataCache.invalidate` (and `clear`) now also detach the request in flight. A request sent before an invalidation can neither answer a later caller nor overwrite a newer answer.
- Every provider path that re-reads objects also drops the adapter entry for each name the provider read through it: `refresh` / `refreshScopes`, `invalidate('object'…)`, an organization switch, and a preview-mode change.
- `invalidateViewKeys` (the one view-write seam) now drops `list:view` as a third key. Any view write through the adapter's client (`saveItem` / `deleteItem` / `publishItem` / `rollbackItem`) also detaches the list request in flight.
- An in-SPA organization switch or session (user) switch clears the adapter's whole metadata cache, in-flight reads included, because the provider now reads objects through it. The first resolution is not a switch.
- The preview client path is untouched and never reads or fills the shared keys.

## Acceptance notes

- **Card acceptance "the 环境 list reads `meta/view` once":** 2 per open after this PR (was 3). The settled-list fix is the follow-up card the seat files.
- **Not filed, inference only:** `PackagesPage` `publishDrafts` emits no metadata-refresh pulse. It rides that follow-up card. `MetadataProvider`'s own caches are not dropped on a session switch; that predates this PR.

## Pins

`packages/app-shell/src/providers/__tests__/MetadataProvider.oneMetadataRead-13044.test.tsx` drives a real `ObjectStackAdapter` (SDK client included) through a fake `fetch` and counts requests by URL:

- (a) provider-first, adapter-first in flight, adapter-first settled, and the `readObjectScope` names path each give one `meta/object/NAME` request;
- (b) console order: the eager view read, then `listViews` + `listViewOverrides`, gives 2 `meta/view` requests; a reader asking while the eager read is held joins it (1). Later reads and `refresh('view')` re-ask; the seam and a direct client `saveItem` detach the in-flight read;
- (c) CONTROL:
  - a provider invalidation and `refresh('object')` re-ask;
  - a view write through the seam re-asks;
  - the provider's `refresh('view')` re-asks;
  - preview reads go to the preview client, with zero adapter requests and nothing cached;
  - each side keeps its shape (normalized, sortability only on the adapter copy, independent copies);
  - an absence is still an answer and a bare 404 is still a failure.

`packages/data-objectstack/src/cache/MetadataCache.share-13044.test.ts` pins `share` (in flight only) and the in-flight detach.

`packages/app-shell/src/providers/__tests__/MetadataProvider.switchDropsAdapter-13044.test.tsx`: an organization switch, an organization switch with a list read in flight, a session switch, and a first-resolution CONTROL.

**Ablations** were each run on a committed HEAD through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which landed the mutation on disk and restored it, with the restore proven by blob hash equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- The provider join was removed (its `readObjectThroughAdapter(name)` arm swapped back to `getClient().meta.getItem`). The (a) pins and the invalidation control went red: 5 failed / 6 passed. Restore blob `f7dcdb9485ee` matched HEAD. The first attempt was a no-op: the tool refused it because the replacement text was already in the anchor, and nothing ran.
- **Round 2** (on committed `3f58d692ab`):
  - (b) `installViewListShare()` removed: 2 failed / 15 passed. Restored to `8ef74198e009`.
  - (c) the switch `clearCache` removed: 3 failed / 14 passed. Restored to `65727bb246e7`.
  - (w) the client view-write detach removed: 1 failed / 16 passed. Restored to `8ef74198e009`.

## Updated pins (deliberate)

- `viewInvalidationSeam.pin.test.ts`, `viewCacheInvalidation.pin.test.ts` and `deleteView.homes.test.ts`: the seam's ordered key list gains `list:view`.
- `viewCacheInvalidation` keeps its control that `listViews` reads the transport on every call. The seam pin names the two lines that drop `list:view`: the client write wrap and the seam.
- The provider test doubles gain `getObjectSchema` and `invalidateCache`, answering from their own by-name door. That is four in `providers/__tests__`, plus eight in `console/__tests__`, `hooks/__tests__` and `views/record-preview`; the surface was widened by ruling `6268839381`.
